title: Inland Sea
concept: A continuous land rim surrounds a large inland sea. Opposing ground forces must travel around the rim while fleets can cross the central lake directly.
difference: The central water is enclosed by a continuous land ring, reversing the emphasis of open-sea maps where water surrounds the land starts.
routes: A connected land ring gives ground forces a long route around the lake and multiple approaches to the opposing side.
A separate, broad inland lake connects both naval ports for a faster direct crossing.
The lake remains separated from the outer ocean so the naval shortcut has a deliberate central focus.
economy: Use mirrored home resources on the ring and distribute expansion metal across the accessible land and central lake.
core_wishes: Registry and watermark assignment by the core integration owner.
